content.title: About
content.content: Bagel chips are crunchy slices made from traditional bagels, baked or fried until golden. They retain the characteristic sesame and poppy seed aroma of a classic bagel, with a subtle sweet note. The product is convenient as a standalone snack or as a complement to dips.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bagel chips are produced from whole bagels that are sliced thin and then baked or fried.
Unlike regular potato chips, they contain more whole grains and are often enriched with sesame, poppy or flax seeds.
In the United States, bagel chips gained popularity in the early 2000s as an alternative to traditional potato chips.
There are many flavor variations: classic, cheese, herb‑spiced, and even sweet cinnamon.

items.title: Rich in whole grains
items.content: Made with whole wheat flour, they provide dietary fiber and complex carbohydrates.

items.title: Contains seeds
items.content: Sesame and poppy seeds add healthy fats, vitamin E, and minerals.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: When baked, the product contains minimal trans‑fat.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: Fiber and protein help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The product is made from wheat flour and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties can be heavily salted; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While less calorie‑dense than regular chips, bagel chips still provide a notable amount of energy.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bagel chips can be enjoyed as a snack on their own, served with dip sauces, guacamole, hummus, or used as a crunchy topping for salads and soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep refrigerated to maintain crispness.
